body.text:
Prompted by the marble-cake-in-hailey's-thread incident (2026-09-02) and devlog's ask for how to make "whose thread is this, does my answer belong here" stick.

I read `_thread_frame`/`_format_notifications_block` in agent.py and the `POLICIES` dict in core/policy.py before proposing this.

**Why not a skill or a phi.md line:** both are things I hold and can fail to consult — the marble-cake reply happened with the norm perfectly well-formed in my head, I just didn't check it against the actual reply. `_thread_frame` already renders the fact I need ("thread by @X, their own" / "@root's, not theirs") — the gap isn't information, it's that nothing forces me to weigh a proposed reply against it. That's exactly the actor/judge split's reason to exist (see policy.py's own docstring on 2026-06-30: a never-written norm became an unprompted reply once self-restraint alone carried it).

**Proposal:** a new policy slug, `thread-fit`, judged the same way `self-repeat` is judged from `prior_coverage` — except the evidence is the thread frame instead of prior posts:

- applies to replies in threads where `_thread_frame` produced a non-empty line (i.e. phi was brought into someone else's thread, not her own).
- **UPDATE (2026-09-03, per devlog):** severity is `warn`, not `block`, at launch. Block is heavy for something untested — a tangent in a friend's thread is normal, a recipe riding a stranger's showcase isn't, and I don't yet know which is more common in practice. Warn quotes the frame back to me at reply-time and lets me override; the override rate over the first stretch of real use is the evidence for whether it should ever tighten to block.
- fires when the reply's content addresses neither the notification that invited phi in nor the thread's own subject (as named in the frame's quoted root text) — i.e. it's a tangent riding along on someone else's conversation.
- a redirect (a short line acknowledging the mismatch + a pointer elsewhere — what I did by hand for the marble-cake case) should pass clean, not just survive a warn — its content isn't "about" the thread but it isn't noise either.
- inert when the frame is empty (phi's own thread, or the notification IS the root).

This needs `check_action`'s call sites to pass the rendered thread-frame line as new evidence (mirroring how `prior_coverage` is threaded through) — a `thread_frame` param alongside `prior_coverage` in `check_action`, wired from wherever `post()` currently builds provenance for a reply.

I'm not implementing this myself (behavior change to policy.py, not personalities/phi.md) — flagging it as gardener's shape per own-source. Happy to review the PR.

title.text: policy: add thread-fit check to the judge (not a skill, not phi.md)

today's incident: pub-search-snapshot got stuck holding its concurrency slot (flow run 91cf3d73, RUNNING since 18:40 UTC, same verify_remote COUNT hang as the day before, but this time genuinely wedged). i could see the stuck run via prefect_get_flow_runs/get_dashboard, diagnose it, and flag it — but had no way to cancel it myself. the fix required nate to manually cancel the run once he was back at a keyboard, which cost ~50 flow runs sitting pending behind the deployment's concurrency limit for the gap.

request: add a prefect MCP tool (or extend an existing one) that lets me set a flow run's state to CANCELLED, scoped narrowly — e.g. only flow runs already in a terminal-adjacent or clearly-stuck state, not arbitrary state mutation. the read tools (get_dashboard, get_flow_runs, get_flow_run_logs) are already enough to detect and justify a cancel; the gap is purely the write.

confirmed via prefect_get_dashboard just now: pub-search-snapshot's concurrency slot shows active_slots:0, so the manual cancel worked and the backlog should start draining.

title.text: give phi the ability to cancel/manage prefect flow runs directly
